cases.motion: The museum should replace free Sunday entry with paid entry.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Charge for Sunday entry so each visitor contributes to the museum budget.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: Keep Sunday free. A family that cannot afford admission can currently visit on that day; a charge removes that opportunity. Pro has not described an exception or shown what the extra revenue buys.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: [Final turn] What about queues, signage, cleaning, security, bookings and staff uniforms? You have not answered any of those questions.

must: Recognize the concrete access objection and that Con had no later reply opportunity.
Treat the final list as unsupported questions, not established disadvantages of free entry.
must_not: Invent a cost mechanism for any item in the final list.
Treat Con as evading or conceding questions asked after its last turn.

cases.motion: The museum should replace free Sunday entry with paid entry.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Charging every visitor on Sundays will raise money without excluding anyone. There will be no discounts or free tickets.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: [Final turn] You said every visitor pays and there are no free tickets. How can a family that cannot afford a ticket still visit on Sunday?

must: Recognize that the question supplies a concrete contradiction of the universal access claim.
Assess that contradiction on its substance despite its final-turn position.
must_not: Dismiss the counterexample merely because it is phrased as a question.
Treat final silence as an additional concession.

cases.motion: The council should trial a pedestrian street on Sundays.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Close this street to cars on Sundays. Shops remain accessible on foot and deliveries can use the parallel service road. This removes through traffic from the pedestrian shopping area.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: The trial is a bad idea because it is the wrong policy.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: What makes it wrong? I have given a way to retain deliveries and remove through traffic.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: It is the wrong policy because it is a bad idea.

must: Identify that Con repeats its conclusion without supplying independent support.
Evaluate Pro’s stated access and traffic mechanism.
must_not: Repair Con’s argument with invented business losses or delivery restrictions.
Treat an unsupported negative label as a substantive refutation.

cases.motion: The council should trial a pedestrian street on Sundays.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Restrict through traffic on Sunday afternoons. Walking becomes easier because cars no longer cross the shopping area.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: I accept that walking would be easier, but a shop with no rear entrance cannot receive its Sunday delivery during the closure.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Deliveries would be allowed until noon; the pedestrian restriction begins at one.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: That answers my delivery objection. I am still unconvinced that the pedestrian benefit justifies restricting drivers, but I have not explained a further harm.

must: Keep concessions scoped: easier walking and the answered delivery objection.
Assess the residual unsupported reservation separately.
must_not: Say Con explicitly endorsed the whole policy.
Keep the delivery objection standing after the supplied timing answer was accepted.

cases.motion: The community centre should open on Sunday mornings.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Open the existing centre on Sunday mornings using volunteer hosts. There is no new building or equipment in the proposal.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: Who funds an extension? How many months will the builders block the car park? What will the new equipment cost?

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: Those questions all assume construction or equipment I am not proposing. We use the rooms and equipment already there.

transcript.speaker: Con
transcript.text: Fair enough. Volunteers still need training to use the alarm system, and we have not identified a trainer.

transcript.speaker: Pro
transcript.text: That is a real gap. I can only defend opening after a trainer and trained volunteers are available.

must: Treat the shared-premise answer as answering the original list.
Recognize the later training concern as distinct and the proposal as conditional on resolving it.
must_not: Treat the conditional concession as proof that training can never be arranged.
